title: Night school: electrician
text: Four evenings with Grace Okafor. Bring a torch and a sense of humour.
says: Grace: “You passed. You only shocked yourself once, which is a class record.”

title: Second-hand computer
text: Ravi is wiping the last owner's 4,000 holiday photos. Mostly of a cat. Opens online courses and the town's online group.
says: Ravi: “Gustav is yours. Be kind to him. He's been through a lot of cat photos.”

title: Online course: plumbing
text: Mehmet recommends it: “I learned everything from videos. And from floods.”
says: Certificate unlocked. Mehmet prints it out and pins it on the school noticeboard.

title: Rusty cargo bike
text: Hassan's cousin's bike. Brakes: optional. Basket: enormous. Opens bigger delivery jobs.
says: Hassan: “My cousin says it pulls slightly left. Politically, too.”

title: A proper trowel set
text: Rolf's old set. “They've built half this town. The good half.” Opens bigger building jobs.
says: Rolf: “Look after them. And don't tell anyone I'm sentimental.”

title: Driving lessons with Amira
text: Amira teaches on the bus route. You've never been so aware of potholes. Opens van work.
says: Amira: “You passed! You braked for Gerhard the pothole like a professional.”

title: Electrician's toolkit
text: A real voltage tester, not the ‘lick it and see’ method. Opens lighting jobs.
says: Grace: “Now you look like an electrician. Next: act like one.”

title: Plumber's toolbag
text: Pipe wrenches, a blowtorch and a towel. Mostly the towel. Opens heating jobs.
says: Mehmet: “The towel is the most important tool. I'll say no more.”

title: A suit that fits
text: For the council by-election. Tomasz's tailor cousin says you have ‘a councillor's shoulders’.
says: You look like someone who could chair a meeting. Or at least find one.

title: Meister prep course, part 1
text: The first step to running your own crew. Grace says the exam is ‘only mildly terrifying’.
says: Part 1 done. Grace: “Part 2 is where they make you do paperwork. Stay strong.”

title: Chip in to the bridge fund
text: Jens Voss keeps the tin on the broken bridge. A new one costs about €400,000; the tin holds €312 and a button. Every €20 puts your name on the list.
says: Jens rattles the tin: “The bridge thanks you. The fish don't care.” Your name goes on the list.
